title: Velocity Inspector — per-route & per-model telemetry blueprint
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a cohesive UI blueprint and high-fidelity prototype for the Velocity Inspector: a combined per-route and per-model performance dashboard focused on latency distributions, throughput over time, token-level metrics, and cost attribution. The inspector will support rapid incident triage, rollout validation, and optimization recommendations. This ticket covers visual specs, interaction patterns (hover drilldowns, trace sampling, anomaly spotlight), accessibility constraints, and handoff artifacts for engineering. Scope excludes backend metric instrumentation and rollout rollout engine implementation (these are in ENG-7120).
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma frames for desktop and tablet covering: overview, anomaly spotlight, token-waterfall inspector, cost attribution view
Chart specs with data schema examples for latency percentiles, throughput bands, token histograms, and KV-cache health glyph
Prototype links that demonstrate hover drilldown, range zoom, trace sampling toggle, and rollout comparison (canary vs baseline)
Accessibility pass checklist completed (contrast, keyboard nav, screen reader labels) and colorblind-safe palette applied
Design handoff doc (Confluence) with annotated tokens, visual tokens, and component variants for engineering
mockups: Frame: Rollout Compare - Canary vs Baseline (desktop)
Frame: Lightweight mobile card - route snapshot
design_decisions: Use combined percentile ribbons (p50/p95/p99) overlaid with median sparkline instead of raw violin per time bucket to reduce visual noise for heavy-traffic routes
Introduce Token-Rail: a horizontally stacked waterfall that aggregates per-token time and cost to help identify token hotspots and KV-cache misses
Anomaly Spotlight aggregates signal sources (latency spikes, error rate bumps, token-cost surges) and surfaces likely root causes with weighted scores—keeps triage in one view
Sampling for full traces is required by default (1% for high-volume routes) with explicit user toggle to capture a higher-fidelity trace window; trade-off balances cost vs. debug fidelity
Prefer canvas-based rendering for the Riverline throughput chart to support 100k+ points and smooth scrubbing; fallback to SVG for small datasets
Color palette follows WCAG AA: use blue-green for healthy ranges, amber for degraded, vermillion for critical; all color states have companion texture or pattern options for colorblind users
tradeoffs: Percentile ribbons vs. small-multiple histograms: ribbons reduce space and make trends easier to compare across routes but hide distribution shape details; histograms exposed in expanded token inspector
Inline cost attribution offers immediate insights but increases query cost; implement coarse-grained cost buckets on overview and provide detailed cost chord only on demand
Full-trace capture provides best debugging info but expensive; adopt adaptive sampling and short-term high-fidelity windows tied to anomaly spikes
Complex interactive controls (range selection, compare toggle, sampling slider) increase cognitive load; add progressive disclosure and templated quick views
review_feedback: PM (Jonah Patel) - prioritize rollout comparison flows; product needs an A/B summary card that executives can read at a glance
Engineering (Ethan Liu) - prefers quantized buckets for density overlays to reduce telemetry cardinality; flagged ENG-7120 for API contract changes
Security (Priya Shah) - asked for notes on PII redaction for trace samples and explicit opt-in for full payload capture
Accessibility (Leah O'Connor) - requested keyboard-first interactions for timeline scrubbing and explicit aria-labels for token-waterfall rows
Design review (Marco Rivera) - suggested a lighter baseline for the overview background to increase contrast of percentile ribbons

metrics_spec: latency.server.p50 - median server processing time in ms (excludes network and client)
latency.server.p95 - 95th percentile server time in ms
latency.server.p99 - 99th percentile server time in ms
throughput.rps - requests per second aggregated to user-selected bucket (default 1m)
tokens.response.avg - average tokens produced per response in selected window
tokens.per_request.histogram - histogram of token counts per response with configurable buckets
cost.per_1k_tokens - derived USD cost per 1000 tokens attributed to route/model and annotation for quantization/kv-cache adjustments
kv_cache.hit_rate - percent of KV cache hits for route-model combination
error.rate - 5xx and client-side error percentage by route
notes_for_engineering: See Confluence page for example payloads and edge-case notes: missing percentile buckets, sparse tokenHistogram arrays
Backend should provide a flag whether KV-cache data is available per-route - UI shows 'KV data unavailable' gracefully
Implement rate-limited trace capture API to support short-term high-fidelity windows triggered by anomaly detection
Charts should support a lightweight mode for low-power devices: reduce point density and disable heavy animations
